newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Amrad signs A$6.5mln gene therapy deal.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Amrad signs A$6.5mln gene therapy deal.

text.p: Australian pharmaceutical company Amrad Corp Ltd said on Tuesday it and the Ludwig Institute for Cancer Research had struck a A$6.5 million deal to supply a gene for a heart disease therapy.
The gene therapy is being developed by U.S.-based Collateral Therapeutics, Amrad said after sealing the deal.
The agreement gives Collateral exclusive use of the gene, patented by Amrad and the Ludwig Institute, to develop the new therapy, Amrad said.

"The agreement involves upfront and milestone payments that exceed the A$6.5 million, plus royalties on any sales that result from the use of the gene for this indication...," Amrad managing director John Grace said in a statement.
Amrad and the Ludwig institute retain rights for all other uses of the gene, known as the human vascular endothelial growth factor B or VEGF-B, he added.

Collateral has shown, using an experimental model, that genes delivered directly to the heart can stimulate the formation of secondary blood vessels, restoring blood flow to oxygen-starved regions of the heart, the statement said.
